description: Experience the ultimate American classic with this New York Strip Steak, perfectly seared to a golden crust and basted in aromatic garlic butter. This recipe guarantees a juicy, tender steak that will rival any steakhouse, making it an ideal centerpiece for your dinner table.

instructions.title: Prepare the Steaks
instructions.text: Remove the New York Strip steaks from the refrigerator at least 30-60 minutes before cooking to bring them to room temperature. Pat the steaks thoroughly dry with paper towels to ensure a good sear. Season generously on all sides with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper.

instructions.title: Heat the Pan
instructions.text: Heat a heavy-bottomed skillet, preferably cast iron, over high heat until it is smoking slightly, about 5-7 minutes. Add the olive oil to the hot pan and swirl to coat the bottom. The oil should shimmer.

instructions.title: Sear the Steaks
instructions.text: Carefully place the seasoned steaks into the hot pan. Sear undisturbed for 3-4 minutes per side for a medium-rare steak, or longer for desired doneness, until a deep golden-brown crust forms. Avoid overcrowding the pan; cook one or two steaks at a time if necessary.

instructions.title: Add Garlic Butter and Aromatics
instructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the cold butter, smashed garlic cloves, rosemary, and thyme sprigs to the pan. Allow the butter to melt and the aromatics to infuse into the butter. Tilt the pan slightly to pool the butter.

instructions.title: Baste the Steaks
instructions.text: Using a spoon, continuously baste the melted garlic butter and aromatics over the steaks for 1-2 minutes, ensuring all surfaces are coated. This enhances flavor and promotes even cooking. Use an instant-read thermometer to check for desired internal temperature: 130-135F for medium-rare.

instructions.title: Rest the Steaks
instructions.text: Remove the steaks from the pan and transfer them to a cutting board. Tent loosely with aluminum foil and let them rest for at least 5-10 minutes. This crucial step allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, ensuring a tender and juicy steak.

instructions.title: Slice and Serve
instructions.text: After resting, slice the New York Strip steaks against the grain into thick pieces. Drizzle any remaining pan juices and garlic butter over the sliced steak. Serve immediately with your favorite American side dishes.

tips: For an authentic American steakhouse crust, ensure your cast iron skillet is smoking hot before adding the steak. This creates the Maillard reaction for deep flavor.
Always use cold butter for basting; it melts slower and emulsifies better with the pan juices, creating a richer sauce. Fresh herbs like rosemary and thyme are essential for flavor.
Resting the steak is non-negotiable for a juicy result. Skipping this step will cause all the delicious juices to run out when you cut into it.
article:
Unlock the secret to a truly unforgettable home-cooked meal with a dish that embodies both elegance and robust flavor: the New York Strip Steak Garlic Butter. This classic American Dinner Recipe takes a prime cut of beef and elevates it with the irresistible aroma and taste of rich, savory garlic butter, promising a culinary experience that’s both simple to achieve and incredibly satisfying. Whether you're planning a special occasion dinner or simply want to treat yourself to a gourmet meal any night of the week, mastering this recipe will make you a kitchen hero.

## What is New York Strip Steak?

The New York Strip Steak, also known as the Ambassador Steak, Kansas City Strip, or just "the strip," is a beloved cut of beef renowned for its excellent balance of flavor and tenderness. Sourced from the short loin of the cow, it’s characterized by its fine grain and a generous amount of marbling, which contributes to its juicy texture and rich, beefy taste. Unlike the more tender filet mignon, the New York Strip offers a bit more chew and a stronger beef flavor, making it a favorite among steak connoisseurs. It often comes with a thin fat cap along one side, which, when rendered properly, adds another layer of flavor and helps keep the steak moist during cooking. Its consistent shape and thickness also make it an ideal candidate for pan-searing and oven-finishing, ensuring even cooking and a beautiful crust.

## Why You'll Love This Garlic Butter Steak

This recipe for New York Strip Steak Garlic Butter isn't just a meal; it's an experience. You'll love it for several compelling reasons. First, the combination of perfectly seared steak with fragrant garlic butter creates an unparalleled depth of flavor that is both comforting and sophisticated. The butter basting technique ensures the steak remains incredibly juicy and tender, infused with garlic and herb notes. Second, it's surprisingly simple to execute, even for novice cooks, yielding restaurant-quality results in your own kitchen. You get to control the quality of ingredients and the doneness, tailoring it precisely to your preference. Finally, it's a versatile dish that can be dressed up for a special occasion or enjoyed as a luxurious weeknight treat. It’s an American Dinner Recipe that consistently delivers on taste, texture, and visual appeal, making it a guaranteed crowd-pleaser.

## Ingredients for Garlic Butter New York Strip

To create this magnificent New York Strip Steak Garlic Butter, you'll need a few key ingredients, most of which you likely already have on hand. The quality of your steak is paramount, so opt for a good cut.

*   **New York Strip Steaks:** 2 (1-1.5 inch thick, about 10-12 oz each)
*   **Olive Oil:** 1-2 tablespoons (for searing)
*   **Salt:** 1-2 teaspoons (coarse sea salt or kosher salt)
*   **Black Pepper:** 1 teaspoon (freshly ground)
*   **Unsalted Butter:** 4-6 tablespoons
*   **Garlic:** 4-6 cloves, minced
*   **Fresh Herbs:** 2-3 sprigs (such as rosemary, thyme, or a mix)

## How to Cook New York Strip Steak with Garlic Butter

Mastering the art of cooking New York Strip Steak Garlic Butter at home is simpler than you might think. Follow these steps for a perfectly seared, buttery, and flavorful steak every time.

1.  **Prepare the Steak:** Remove the steaks from the refrigerator at least 30-60 minutes before cooking to allow them to come closer to room temperature. This promotes more even cooking. Pat them thoroughly dry with paper towels – moisture is the enemy of a good sear. Season generously on all sides with salt and freshly ground black pepper. Don't be shy; a good crust needs plenty of seasoning.

2.  **Heat the Pan:** Place a heavy-bottomed skillet (cast iron is ideal) over high heat. Let it heat for 3-5 minutes until it's smoking slightly. Add the olive oil and swirl to coat the pan. You want a very hot pan to achieve a beautiful sear.

3.  **Sear the Steaks:** Carefully place the seasoned steaks in the hot pan. Sear undisturbed for 2-4 minutes per side, depending on thickness and desired doneness. You're looking for a deep, golden-brown crust. Use tongs to sear the edges as well, especially the fat cap, rendering it down slightly.

4.  **Add Garlic Butter:** Reduce the heat to medium. Now, for the magic of the New York Strip Steak Garlic Butter. Add the unsalted butter, minced garlic, and fresh herb sprigs to the pan. Once the butter melts, tilt the pan slightly and use a large spoon to continuously baste the melted garlic butter over the steaks for 1-2 minutes. This infuses the steak with incredible flavor and helps to finish cooking it.

5.  **Check Doneness:** Use an instant-read meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of the steak (avoiding bone or fat) to check for desired doneness:
    *   Rare: 125-130°F (52-54°C)
    *   Medium-Rare: 130-135°F (54-57°C)
    *   Medium: 135-140°F (57-60°C)
    *   Medium-Well: 140-145°F (60-63°C)
    Remember, the internal temperature will rise a few degrees during resting.

6.  **Rest the Steaks:** Transfer the steaks to a cutting board or plate. Tent loosely with foil and let them rest for at least 5-10 minutes. This crucial step allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, resulting in a more tender and juicy steak.

7.  **Serve:** Slice against the grain, if desired, and serve immediately, spooning any remaining garlic butter from the pan over the top.

## Expert Tips for Perfect Steak

Achieving a perfect New York Strip Steak Garlic Butter consistently involves a few key techniques:

*   **Room Temperature Steak:** Don't skip bringing your steak to room temperature. A cold steak cooks unevenly, resulting in a gray band in the center.
*   **Pat Dry:** Moisture creates steam, preventing a good crust. Always pat your steaks thoroughly dry.
*   **High Heat Sear:** A screaming hot pan is essential for developing that desirable crispy, flavorful crust.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Pan:** Cook steaks one at a time or in batches if your pan isn't large enough. Overcrowding lowers the pan temperature and leads to steaming, not searing.
*   **Use a Thermometer:** Visual cues can be misleading. An instant-read thermometer is your best friend for achieving perfect doneness every time.
*   **Resting is Non-Negotiable:** This is arguably the most important step for a juicy steak. Skipping it will result in juices running out onto your plate instead of remaining in the meat.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

The robust flavor of New York Strip Steak Garlic Butter pairs beautifully with a variety of sides, making it a versatile center for any American Dinner Recipes menu. For a classic steakhouse experience, serve it alongside creamy mashed potatoes or a baked potato loaded with chives and sour cream. Roasted asparagus, green beans almandine, or sautéed mushrooms are excellent vegetable accompaniments that add freshness and texture. A simple side salad with a vinaigrette dressing can also cut through the richness of the steak. For wine pairings, a bold Cabernet Sauvignon or a robust Merlot will complement the rich beefiness and garlic notes perfectly. If you prefer beer, a stout or a malty ale would be a delightful match.

## Variations and FAQs

**Q: Can I use different herbs?**
A: Absolutely! While rosemary and thyme are classic, feel free to experiment with sage, oregano, or even a touch of fresh parsley for different flavor profiles in your New York Strip Steak Garlic Butter.

**Q: What if I don't have a cast-iron skillet?**
A: Any heavy-bottomed, oven-safe skillet will work. Stainless steel pans are a good alternative, though cast iron offers superior heat retention.

**Q: Can I finish the steak in the oven?**
A: Yes, if your steaks are thicker (1.5 inches or more), you can sear them for 2-3 minutes per side, then transfer the pan to a preheated 375°F (190°C) oven for 5-10 minutes to finish cooking to your desired doneness, before adding the garlic butter for basting on the stovetop.

**Q: How can I make this spicier?**
A: Add a pinch of red pepper flakes to the garlic butter for a subtle kick.

**Q: What's the best way to store leftovers?**
A: Store any leftover New York Strip Steak Garlic Butter in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days. Reheat gently to avoid overcooking.

With this comprehensive guide, you’re ready to impress yourself and your loved ones with a restaurant-quality New York Strip Steak Garlic Butter right in your own kitchen. It's a truly satisfying American Dinner Recipe that's sure to become a cherished part of your culinary repertoire. Enjoy the rich flavors and the simple elegance of this perfectly prepared steak!
